0.0.n: 最後に introduces the final question or request.

0.1.n: Combines with 最後 to mean lastly or at the end.

0.2.n: A general counter for one item; here it refers to one more question.

0.3.n: いい plus polite です asks permission here; the action of asking is left unstated.

0.4.n: Placed at the end to turn the sentence into a question.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the wish being asked about.

1.2.n: Before したい, it indicates the strongest desire.

1.3.n: する becomes したい by replacing ます in します with たい to express desire.

1.4.n: Turns したい into a noun phrase: the thing someone wants to do.

1.5.n: Marks the thing most wanted as the topic of the question.

1.6.n: Read as なん before です; asks which activity the person wants to do.

2.0.n: The speaker explicitly identifies themselves before stating their wish.

2.1.n: Marks 私 as the topic: the speaker's own wish follows.

2.2.n: Japanese leaves my unstated because the speaker's family is understood.

2.3.n: Marks the people the speaker wants to meet, used with 会う.

2.4.n: 会う becomes 会いたい to express desire; です makes the statement polite.

3.0.n: Identifies the speaker as the person expressing a wish.

3.1.n: Sets 私 as the topic of the statement.

3.2.n: Written in katakana, this names the noodle dish the speaker wants.

3.3.n: With たい, が can mark what someone wants to eat; を is also possible.

3.4.n: 食べる becomes 食べたい to express desire; です adds politeness.

4.0.n: Identifies who intends to make the confession.

4.1.n: Marks the speaker as the topic before announcing their plan.

4.2.n: 恋人 normally means an existing partner, not a crush, so the supplied English is loose here.

4.3.n: Marks the person who will receive the confession.

4.4.n: 告白 plus polite します announces an intended action, rather than a wish with たい.

5.0.n: Imitates cheering or whistling, here playfully reacting to the romantic announcement.

5.2.n: The て-form of 頑張る works as a casual request or encouragement to do one's best.

5.3.n: Adds warmth and support to the encouragement.

6.0.n: Addresses the whole group respectfully; さん adds courtesy.

6.2.n: The prefix お adds respect to 時間, referring to the listeners' time.

6.3.n: The core expression of gratitude, made more formal by the following ございました.

6.4.n: ござい is part of ございます, which makes ありがとう more formal.

6.5.n: まし is the part of ます used before た in the polite past ending ました.

6.6.n: Completes ございました, thanking people for time they have already given.

7.0.n: Refers to the present point in the broadcast.

7.1.n: In これで, marks this point as the occasion for bringing something to a close.

7.2.n: Refers to the broadcast segment being transmitted from the location.

7.3.n: Marks 中継 as what the speaker is bringing to an end.

7.4.n: Polite form of 終わる, used here with を to announce closing the broadcast.

0.lit: Lastly, one thing, is it okay?
0.tip: 一ついいですか politely asks permission to ask one question without explicitly saying ask.

1.lit: Now, as for the thing you most want to do, what is it?
1.tip: したいこと means the thing you want to do: こと turns the preceding phrase into a noun.

2.lit: As for me, I want to meet my family.
2.tip: Use に to mark the person you meet with 会う.

3.lit: As for me, ramen is what I want to eat.
3.tip: With a たい wish, が can mark the desired object instead of を.

4.lit: As for me, I will confess my feelings to my romantic partner!
4.tip: します announces a planned action here, unlike したいです, which expresses a wish.

5.tip: A verb's て-form can stand alone as a casual request or encouragement.

6.tip: ありがとうございました uses the polite past form to thank people for something already received.

7.lit: With this, I will end the live broadcast.
7.tip: これで is a common way to signal that an event or activity is concluding.
